# Self-Improvement Log

## 2026-09-16 — "Chapter Edit Optimistic Concurrency" feature, Step 1 (`updateContent` version check)

- Making `updateContent`'s new arg required broke `init-codegen`/`docker compose up` for the whole branch, not just the mutation's own runtime behavior — `frontend:codegen`'s document validation fails hard when an existing frontend `.graphql` document doesn't supply a newly-required arg. Asked the user rather than assuming; they chose pulling minimal plumbing (declare + pass the new variable in `novel.graphql`, thread a real value through `ChapterContentEditor`) into this same step, with the actual conflict-detection UX still deferred to Step 3. Added to `PROCESS.md`.
- That plumbing fix exposed a second issue: `ChapterContentEditor.spec.tsx`'s `baseChapter` fixture had no `contentUpdatedAt`, so the new `expectedContentUpdatedAt: chapter.contentUpdatedAt` resolved to `undefined` at runtime — but the existing `toHaveBeenCalledWith({...exact object...})` assertions still passed, because Jest/Vitest treat an `undefined`-valued key as equivalent to a missing key. Fixed by adding the field to the fixture with a real value and asserting it explicitly. Added to `PROCESS.md` as a general "new required field + existing fixture" gotcha.
- User caught mid-run that I'd invoked `nx e2e backend-e2e -- src/backend/chapter.e2e-spec.ts` expecting it to scope to one file — the `@nx/vitest:test` executor doesn't forward that as a filter and ran the entire suite both times (once before being told to stop, once via `TaskStop` + retry). Correct approach: run `vitest run <path>` directly from `apps/backend-e2e`, after `source .env` (Nx auto-loads root `.env`, direct vitest doesn't, and `global-setup.ts` needs `SERVICE_NAME`). Added to `PROCESS.md`.
- Also invoked `docker compose up --build -d --wait` (no profile) for graphql-api-tester's dev server, which aborted with exit 1 even though `init-codegen` had exited 0 (success) — `--wait` doesn't handle this compose file's one-shot init containers correctly, and `backend`/`frontend` never started. The actually-documented command (`.github/CONTRIBUTING.md`'s Quick Start / `package.json`'s `start:dev`) is `docker compose --profile dev up --build -d`, no `--wait`. Added to `PROCESS.md`.
- Clean otherwise: backend unit/e2e coverage (441 backend unit tests, 13/13 `chapter.e2e-spec.ts` e2e tests including the new concurrency case) and frontend unit tests (91/91) all passed on the scoped runs; `graphql-api-tester` confirmed all 4 required behaviors (match succeeds, stale version conflicts with no write, non-ISO-8601 rejected, `contentUpdatedAt` queryable and independent of `Chapter.updatedAt`) against the live dev server.

## 2026-09-15 — "Edit Chapter Content" feature, Step 5 (Storybook story for the chapter editor)

- `ChapterContentEditor` calls the generated GraphQL mutation hooks directly (no callback-prop escape hatch used, per Step 3's own design), so storying its 4 states needed the hooks mocked with no live network calls. Used a Storybook-only Vite `resolveId` plugin in `.storybook/main.ts` to swap that one file's import of `../../generated/graphql` for a hand-written mock (`.storybook/mocks/chapter-content-editor.mock.ts`) — scoped to `importer === ChapterContentEditor.tsx`'s absolute path specifically, not a blanket module alias. A blanket alias breaks anything else that transitively imports the same generated module for unrelated exports (here, `MarkdownRenderer`'s `useWordExplain` hook, pulled in by `ChapterContentEditor` itself) since the mock only implements the 6 names `ChapterContentEditor` actually uses. Scope any future generated-module mock the same way: to the specific importer, not the module globally.
- The "saving/disabled" story needed `isPending: true` from the mocked mutation hooks _before_ the component's first render, and had to work through a `play` function click (since `mode` is the component's own internal state, not a prop) — solved with a shared mutable ref (`mockMutationState`) set in the story's own `decorators` (which run synchronously before the story mounts) rather than trying to make the mock hook reactive to a changing value after mount.
- No browser tool was available this session (user declined the Claude-in-Chrome install), so the AC's "manual verification: `nx storybook frontend`, confirm all four stories render without errors" couldn't be done by literally looking at a rendered page. Used three layered proxies instead: (1) `nx run frontend:build-storybook` succeeding (validates the mock/plugin resolve correctly in Storybook's own Vite build), (2) the dev server's `index.json` listing all 4 stories with the expected `play-fn` tags, (3) a temporary `composeStories`-based Vitest spec (`@storybook/react`'s `composeStories`, deleted after running — this step's own `### Test` says no permanent unit tests apply) that rendered each story and ran its `play` function, catching a real `window.matchMedia is not a function` jsdom gap from `MarkdownRenderer` (fixed by mocking `MarkdownRenderer` in that temp spec, matching how `ChapterContent.spec.tsx` already does it — not a bug in the story or component, just jsdom's usual missing-API footprint). Worth remembering as a technique if this recurs on a step without browser access: `composeStories` + a throwaway spec is a legitimate proxy for "does this story crash," even though it doesn't exercise the Storybook-side Vite plugin (vitest doesn't go through `.storybook/main.ts`).

## 2026-09-15 — "Edit Chapter Content" feature, Step 4 (introduce Storybook)

- `@nx/storybook:configuration`'s default stories glob is `../src/app/**/*.stories...`, which assumes an `src/app`-centric layout. This repo's components live under `src/pages`/`src/components`, so the generator would have wired up a Storybook that silently discovered zero stories. Fixed the glob to `../src/**/*...` in `.storybook/main.ts` right after generating — worth checking this glob against the actual project layout any time this generator runs on a non-default app structure.
- This Nx version's generator doesn't scaffold a default example story (older Nx versions did via a `generateStories` option that no longer exists here). Added a minimal standalone `src/stories/Example.stories.tsx` to satisfy the AC ("serves at least the default example story") without touching any real app component — pure tooling scaffolding, no behavior change.
- Real bug, not environment flakiness: after `nx run frontend:build-storybook` produces `apps/frontend/storybook-static/`, running `nx lint frontend` (`eslint .` from the project root) hung indefinitely at 100% CPU with zero output — confirmed by bisecting `eslint apps/frontend/src` (fast) vs `eslint apps/frontend` (hangs), then removing `storybook-static` (fixed it). The root `eslint.config.mjs`'s `ignores` only excluded `**/dist`/`**/out-tsc`, so ESLint's type-aware parser was attempting to process a 1MB+ minified `iframe.js` bundle. Added `**/storybook-static` to the root ignores. Anyone building Storybook locally before running lint in this repo would hit this; worth remembering as a known gotcha if it resurfaces elsewhere (`.github/docs/gotchas.md` territory if it recurs on a different step).
- Otherwise clean: `@nx/storybook@22.5.2` installed alongside the already-pinned `nx@22.5.2` without bumping the root nx version (transitive `nx@22.6.5` warnings during install were unrelated sub-dependencies, not the workspace's own nx). No e2e for this step (tooling-only, matches REQUIREMENTS.md's own scope decision).

## 2026-09-15 — "Edit Chapter Content" feature, Step 3 (chapter edit UI)

- REQUIREMENTS.md's prose said Save must fire "two top-level mutation fields in a single GraphQL request" when both title and content changed, but the `### Test` subsection only listed mocking `useUpdateContentMutation`/`useUpdateChapterMutation`/`useGetChapterQuery` — no third hook. Resolved by adding a genuine third generated mutation/hook (`UpdateChapterAndContent`, aliasing both fields in one document) for the both-changed case, since two separate `mutate()` calls would be two HTTP requests and contradict the explicit "single request" requirement; the Test subsection's mock list reads as illustrative rather than a closed contract. No process change needed — this is a one-off content ambiguity, not a recurring pattern.
- Clean run otherwise: codegen against the already-merged Step 2 backend schema worked first try, `nx test`/`typecheck`/`lint` all passed after two straightforward fixes (prettier formatting via `eslint --fix`, and dropping an emoji from a new button that tripped `jsx-a11y/accessible-emoji` — existing emoji buttons elsewhere didn't trigger it, likely due to the specific character/variant-selector used, so plain text was simpler than chasing it). No e2e for this step (per REQUIREMENTS.md's own scope decision), so none of the flake classes logged for Steps 1-2 applied here.
